forward: sort establishes total evaluation and presentation order
tie_determinism=total because (k,id) is unique
limit preserves the ordered prefix and sets exact bounded cardinality
backward: final sequence observer demands values, schema, cardinality, and presentation order
limit propagates evaluation-order demand to sort
sort discharges it with a total key
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: sequence exact + schema exact + cardinality exact
workflow_derivations.unknown_or_failure: duplicate total keys or unknown uniqueness downgrades tie_determinism; it does not silently switch the whole result to bag

workflow_derivations.workflow: sort(k non-total) -> limit(n) with a tie crossing n
forward: sort establishes key partial order
tie_determinism=non_total
limit cuts an observable tie class
backward: limit demands evaluation order and exact n
observer demands membership in the legal top-k set but not a particular within-tie row
rows outside the boundary tie remain fixed
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: partial-order legal-top-k membership + exact cardinality + exact non-tie components
workflow_derivations.unknown_or_failure: bag equality is too strict for legal tie choices and ignoring all rows is too weak

workflow_derivations.workflow: limit(n) on an input with no cross-backend order contract
forward: evaluation_order=unknown
presentation_order=unknown
cardinality is bounded but membership is not uniquely determined
backward: limit requires an upstream evaluation order to prove cross-backend membership
no rule discharges that demand
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: cardinality-only observation; value equivalence is INCONCLUSIVE unless an endpoint-scoped input-order rule applies
workflow_derivations.unknown_or_failure: must not label arbitrary differing prefixes SATISFIED

workflow_derivations.workflow: running_sum(partition, order_by) -> join with duplicate matches
forward: running_sum consumes partition/evaluation order and computes exact cumulative values
join preserves computed values and multiplicity semantics but kills final presentation order
tie determinism remains an internal precondition only
backward: final bag observer does not demand presentation order
it still demands exact running_sum values
running_sum propagates partition/evaluation-order demand to its input
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: bag exact values + exact join multiplicities; no final row-sequence relation
workflow_derivations.unknown_or_failure: this is the approved precision fix for the four running_sum_precision rows

forward: running_sum has internal ordered evaluation
join kills prior presentation order
final total sort re-establishes presentation order
backward: sequence observer demands the final sort order
numeric values still demand the running_sum partition order
the two order demands remain distinct
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: sequence exact + numeric exact + independent evaluation-order precondition

forward: groupby kills input/presentation order
group membership uses an explicit NULL grouping relation
each aggregate has its own null-skip, empty/all-null, dtype, and numeric rule
backward: bag observer demands exact group keys and one output row per group
aggregate outputs demand only their input columns and declared null policy
input duplicate multiplicity remains observable through aggregate values/counts
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: bag exact groups + per-aggregate component relations + exact cardinality
workflow_derivations.unknown_or_failure: a backend without the declared aggregate/null semantics is INAPPLICABLE, not tolerated globally

forward: input duplicate multiplicity is killed
output uniqueness postcondition requires multiplicity exactly one per projected row
presentation order is generally unobserved
backward: observer demands set membership and output uniqueness
it does not demand preservation of input counts
cardinality equals the number of unique projected rows
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: set membership + uniqueness postcondition + exact cardinality
workflow_derivations.unknown_or_failure: plain set comparison alone would hide a backend that incorrectly emits duplicates

workflow_derivations.workflow: inner_join(left,right,on=keys) with duplicate and unmatched keys
forward: matched multiplicity is the product of left/right key multiplicities
unmatched rows are absent
presentation order is killed
NULL-key equality is a separately selected relation
backward: bag observer demands exact joined values and multiplicities
key/value demand propagates to both inputs
no sequence demand propagates without a final order observer
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: bag exact + join multiplicity + explicit NULL-key relation

forward: each qualifying left row is emitted once
right multiplicity is semantically ignored
left multiplicity is preserved
NULL membership is explicit
backward: observer demands left-row bag membership
right side is demanded only as an existence predicate
right payload and duplicate counts are unobserved
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: left-bag filtering by existential membership + right-duplicate invariance

forward: left rows without a match are emitted once per left occurrence
right duplicates do not change output
anti_join semantics are not automatically SQL NOT IN semantics
backward: observer demands complement membership and left multiplicity
right side is demanded only for existence/non-existence
NULL policy is operation-specific
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: left-bag complement + right-duplicate invariance + explicit NULL membership

workflow_derivations.workflow: mutate(cast(s -> int)) where every value is in the common domain
forward: definedness=defined under lexical/range preconditions
result logical dtype and nullability are known
value conversion is exact
backward: value/dtype observer demands source values and cast rule
unobserved source columns can be projected away
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: exact tagged values + exact logical dtype/nullability

workflow_derivations.workflow: mutate(cast(s -> int)) with invalid or out-of-range input
forward: definedness is semantic-domain-error only when the common contract specifies rejection
unsupported capability, timeout, crash, and adapter failure remain distinct
backward: status observer requests error category and relevant input/range facts
value rows are not requested for a rejected endpoint
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: exact accept/reject plus scoped semantic-error category
workflow_derivations.unknown_or_failure: different undocumented behavior yields INCONCLUSIVE; timeout/crash never becomes unsupported

forward: lossless observations retain sign bit
arithmetic, equality, ordering, grouping, and serialization roles are separate facts
backward: exact numeric observer demands sign when the operation can expose it
an equality-predicate observer may legally identify the zeros only under its own rule
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: role-specific tagged exact or explicit signed-zero equivalence

forward: NaN, infinities, NULL, and finite values remain distinct tagged classes
predicate truth, ordering, grouping, aggregate propagation, and conversion are independent components
backward: only roles feeding the final observer are demanded
a NaN sort rule cannot weaken aggregate or NULL equality

workflow_derivations.workflow: same Arrow logical table, contiguous vs non-zero-offset slice
forward: layout changes offset/buffer view
logical schema, values, cardinality, and order are preserved by the layout transform
backward: layout-equivalence observer demands exact logical values/schema and activation evidence that slice_offset>0
physical offset is the changed axis, not a permitted value difference
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: layout equivalence with exact logical sequence/bag selected by the program contract

workflow_derivations.workflow: same Arrow logical table split into multiple chunks
forward: chunk boundaries change physical partitioning only
logical concatenated values and schema are preserved
backward: observer demands chunk_count>=2 activation plus exact logical output
partition order of chunks is retained unless a later semantic operation changes order

workflow_derivations.workflow: plain vs dictionary-encoded column with the same decoded values
forward: indices/dictionary are physical representation
decoded value sequence, null bitmap semantics, and logical field semantics are demanded
dictionary ordering flag is not row presentation order
backward: observer demands dictionary activation and decoded exact values
dictionary index assignments and dictionary entry order are unobserved unless the tested kernel explicitly exposes them
workflow_derivations.compiled_relation: dictionary representation invariance + exact decoded values/schema

workflow_derivations.workflow: same typed workflow executed eager, lazy, and streaming
forward: execution mode changes planning/materialization metadata
semantic value/order/schema facts follow the operation rules
unsupported operations are capability evidence
backward: mode-equivalence observer demands the same semantic components for all applicable modes
plan text and timing are evidence metadata, not equality components
workflow_derivations.unknown_or_failure: a streaming mode missing a required operation is INAPPLICABLE with frozen evidence
